name: First Task
summary: Covers the new user's experience from creating their first task through marking it complete. Users arrive with genuine curiosity but the absence of any onboarding or tutorial means many explore aimlessly and do not fully understand the feature set before dropping off.

stages.name: Create Task
actions: Optionally sets a due date or priority
thoughts: Should I add everything now or just one thing to try it out?
I wonder what all these other buttons do

emotions.label: Curious
emotions.description: Engaged and willing to explore, but slightly uncertain about the right way to use the app

painPoints: No prompts or examples to help users understand how to structure their first task
Advanced options (priority, tags, subtasks) are visible immediately and feel overwhelming to new users
opportunities: Show a pre-populated example task on first launch so users see the expected format
Progressive disclosure — hide advanced fields behind a 'More options' toggle for first-time users

stages.name: Explore Interface
actions: Looks for a way to organise tasks into groups
thoughts: What does the Calendar view do?
Can I sort these tasks somehow?
There must be a way to group them

emotions.label: Curious
emotions.description: Actively exploring but without a guide the exploration feels undirected and occasionally confusing

painPoints: No onboarding or tutorial — users discover features by accident rather than by design
Navigation labels are generic ('Lists', 'Inbox') and do not convey what belongs where
No in-context tooltips or coach marks on first use
opportunities: Implement a guided first-task flow with three coach marks highlighting the core actions
Rename navigation tabs to reflect user intent ('My Tasks', 'Due Today', 'All Lists')
Add a dismissable 'Getting started' checklist to the home screen

stages.name: Complete Task
touchpoints: Taskly app — home screen task list
actions: Returns to the task they created
Taps the checkbox to mark it complete
thoughts: That felt good — I actually did it
Where did the task go? Did it get deleted?
I want to see what I have completed so far

emotions.label: Curious
emotions.description: Positive reaction to the completion interaction, but immediately curious about where completed tasks are stored

painPoints: Completed tasks disappear from the default view with no obvious way to find them again
No congratulatory moment or progress indication to reinforce the habit loop on day one
opportunities: Show a 'Completed today' count on the home screen after the first task is marked done
Add a brief guided prompt after the first completion pointing to the completed tasks view

insights.text: 5 of 8 usability participants could not find completed tasks after marking one done — they assumed the app had deleted it
Day-1 retention is 28% lower for users who do not complete at least one task in their first session — task completion in session one is the strongest predictor of week-1 retention
3 of 6 interview participants described the interface as 'a bit overwhelming at first' — all three had not used a dedicated task manager before
